missing_pieces.duty: Authoring gap in a read-only host for 2003-C001/C002. handbook/parts/p13/presentations/abelard-and-contemporaries.tex (and its annex) is routed and substantial, but it does not reconstruct every argument case or example in Wilks's MS ch.3, pp.83-151. Missing: the Porretan 'man and an ass' example and the counterexample practice (MS pp.144-145); the boundary between Alberic's term-logic recasting and the Porretan/Melidunensian propositional treatment (p.144); the Melidunensian false-antecedent argument (p.145); the Parvipontanian crab/rose/lily quotation and the five-step man/stone argument of n.109 in the source's own terms (p.145); Adam of Balsham's first use of 'enuntiabile' and the Socratem legere example (p.146); the implicational vs inferential construal and the Montani's general conditional form (p.148); the absence of a comparable school division on Aristotelian elements (p.149); de Rijk's imposition contrast and the ex diversis adiunctis quotation (pp.149-150); the concrete topic examples (pp.130-133); and the footnote apparatus. A follow-up authoring packet that owns this file is needed.

Authoring gap in a read-only host for 2001/2002-C001/C002 (handbook/parts/p13/presentations/early-medieval-latin-logic.tex). Ch.1 is compressed: missing are Abbo's 'lifeless body' claim, his fire/contraries argument, his third-mode example and Schupp's source argument (MS p.42), and Richer's curriculum detail and Gerbert's 'what is rational uses reason' problem as stated (pp.40-41). Ch.2 is missing the Arnulf of Laon argument (p.75), Green-Pedersen's Master W. attribution and Hansen 2005 (p.79), and the full manuscript catalogue with witnesses and editions (pp.68-69). The manuscript's unfinished-state variants ('page refs', '000-000', 'details to be supplied', 'In XXX') are not recorded.

Authoring gap in a read-only host for 2008-C001/C002 (handbook/parts/p13/presentations/medieval-latin-inference.tex). Missing source qualifications: the Paris/Prague nations, the papal-schism reason Italians studied at Oxford, the founding roles of Albert of Saxony and Marsilius of Inghen, the 1384 Vienna re-foundation (Langenstein, Oyta, Kalkar), and Thomas of Cleves at St Stephen's (MS pp.435-436, nn.1-6). Also missing: Martin of Alnwick as de Rijk's earlier proofs-of-terms text (p.466). A full page-by-page audit of the remaining examples is owed.

2004-C001/C002: handbook/parts/p13/presentations/medieval-supposition-theories.tex (283 lines, labelled 2004) exists but is not \input in handbook/parts/p13.tex and has no annex. It is another packet's file and is not credited. Routing is pending, and its completeness against Parsons MS pp.157-280 has not been assessed.

2005, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 (C001/C002) have no treatment on the route. Their sources are held in the Fordham manuscript: Lagerlund pp.281-346, van der Lecq pp.347-388, Klima pp.389-431, Knuuttila pp.505-578, Yrjonsuuri pp.579-608, Ashworth pp.609-643, Dvorak pp.645-665, Wahl pp.667-699. Each chapter needs new authoring packets and owned files (canonical destinations handbook/parts/p13/presentations/src063-20NN.tex) plus routing.

The final published 2008 volume is not held: Handbook of the History of Logic vol. 2, Mediaeval and Renaissance Logic, ed. Gabbay and Woods, Elsevier/North-Holland 2008, chapters 1-13, pp.1-699. Only the separately identified 726-page Fordham Volume 2.dvi manuscript (source/references/p13-medieval-latin/HHL-Volume2-fordham.pdf, sha 79df3522...) is held. This blocks all 39 components ED26-SRC-063-0201..0213-C001..C003. It also blocks the 'compare both complete bodies with the final 2008 chapter' part of 2001/2002/2003/2008-C002, and duty US-0 (which also names unheld original editions, e.g. Abelard, Dialectica, ed. de Rijk 1970).

US-2: none of the 26 proposed canonical destination files src 063-0201..0213/2001..2013.tex exists. Separate version identities are retained only for 2001-2003 and 2008, in differently named files. US-1 stays partial until chapters 4-7 and 9-13 get full treatments.
